practiceQuestions.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Scheduled and Tribal Areas?
practiceQuestions.sol: Part X of the Indian Constitution, containing Article 244 and Article 244A, is entitled 'The Scheduled and Tribal Areas'.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to declare an area to be a Scheduled Area?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 244(1) applies the provisions of the Fifth Schedule to the Scheduled Areas in any State other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, wherein the President has the power to declare any area as a Scheduled Area.

practiceQuestions.q: How many states currently come under the purview of the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sixth Schedule under Article 244(2) contains provisions for the administration of tribal areas in four north-eastern states: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies is mandatory for every state having Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Fifth Schedule, each state having Scheduled Areas must establish a Tribal Advisory Council (TAC) to advise on welfare and advancement of scheduled tribes.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to alter, increase, or decrease the area of any Sixth Schedule Autonomous District?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Paragraph 1 of the Sixth Schedule, the Governor is empowered to divide the area into autonomous districts, increase or decrease their areas, unite them, or define their boundaries.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum strength specified for a Tribal Advisory Council (TAC) under the Fifth Schedule?
practiceQuestions.sol: A Tribal Advisory Council consists of not more than 20 members, of whom three-fourths shall be the representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of the State.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, an Autonomous District Council (ADC) normally consists of how many members?
practiceQuestions.sol: Paragraph 2 of the Sixth Schedule provides that each Autonomous District Council shall consist of not more than 30 members, out of whom not more than 4 are nominated by the Governor and the rest are elected on the basis of adult suffrage.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment added the Bodo Territorial Council under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution?
opts: No amendment needed; done via Presidential Order
It was established within Assam through memorandums and autonomous provisions under the Sixth Schedule structure
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sixth Schedule lists specific autonomous districts in Assam (North Cachar Hills, Karbi Anglong, and Bodoland Territorial Region), Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. The Bodo Territorial Council (BTC) was formed via a Memorandum of Settlement in 2003 by amending the Sixth Schedule elements for Assam.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of members elected to an Autonomous District Council under the Sixth Schedule, unless dissolved earlier?
practiceQuestions.sol: The elected members of an Autonomous District Council hold office for a term of 5 years from the date appointed for the first meeting of the Council, unless the Council is dissolved earlier.

practiceQuestions.q: Who possesses the ultimate power to direct that any particular Act of Parliament or the State Legislature does not apply to a Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule?
opts: The Chief Minister of the State
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Fifth Schedule (paragraph 5), the Governor may direct that any particular Act of Parliament or the State Legislature does not apply to a Scheduled Area or applies with specified exceptions and modifications.

practiceQuestions.q: How do Fifth Schedule Areas fundamentally differ from Sixth Schedule Areas in terms of administrative autonomy?
opts: Fifth Schedule areas have legislative and judicial powers through ADCs, while Sixth Schedule areas are run directly by the Union Government.

Sixth Schedule areas enjoy high degree of autonomy with Autonomous District Councils having legislative, judicial, and executive powers, whereas Fifth Schedule areas rely heavily on Governor's executive orders and Tribal Advisory Councils.
There is no difference; both schedules grant exact identical local self-governance structures.
Fifth Schedule areas are restricted to North-East India, while Sixth Schedule areas are spread across peninsular India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sixth Schedule provides for self-governance through Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) and Regional Councils with specific law-making, judicial, and taxing powers. The Fifth Schedule focuses on protection against exploitation through executive governance and advisory bodies, lacking distinct ADCs.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the role of the Governor under the Fifth Schedule regarding regulations for peace and good governance. What is the constitutional mandate concerning laws made by the Governor?
opts: They require immediate assent from the Supreme Court.
They must be submitted to the President and have effect only upon receiving the President's assent.
They take effect immediately without any higher approval, bypassing the President.
They can only be promulgated if approved by two-thirds of the Lok Sabha.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Paragraph 5(2) of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor may make regulations for the peace and good governance of any area in a State which is for the time being a Scheduled Area, but such regulations must be submitted to the President and shall have effect only when assented to by the President.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of the 'Autonomous Region' under the Sixth Schedule?
opts: It is created within an autonomous district when there are different tribes, and a Regional Council is constituted for it.
It denotes a Union Territory managed directly by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
It represents a Scheduled Area situated in central peninsular India.
It is an administrative division created exclusively for non-tribal settlers in the North-East.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Paragraph 1(2) of the Sixth Schedule, if there are different tribes in an autonomous district, the Governor may divide the area into autonomous regions and establish a separate Regional Council for each such region.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of judicial administration in Sixth Schedule areas, what powers are granted to Autonomous District Councils?
opts: They can try all criminal cases involving capital punishment without any exception.
They can constitute Village Councils or Courts to try suits and cases between the parties all belonging to Scheduled Tribes, subject to the Governor's control.
They exercise complete appellate jurisdiction over the decisions of the Supreme Court of India.
They do not possess any judicial or quasi-judicial powers whatsoever.
practiceQuestions.sol: Paragraph 4 of the Sixth Schedule empowers ADCs to constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases between parties all of whom belong to Scheduled Tribes within their districts, excluding serious offenses, under specified rules.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Fifth Schedule protect land belonging to Scheduled Tribes from non-tribals?
opts: By prohibiting the purchase of land by non-tribals and restricting transfer of land from tribal to non-tribal persons through Governor's regulations.
By nationalizing all forest produce and handing ownership entirely to the corporate sector.
By dissolving state high courts and handing property rights to village heads.
By banning any economic activity or farming in Scheduled Areas.
practiceQuestions.sol: Governors of states with Scheduled Areas utilize their rule-making power under the Fifth Schedule to prohibit or restrict the transfer of land by or among members of the Scheduled Tribes, preventing alienation of tribal land to non-tribals.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the relationship between the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996 and the Fifth Schedule?
opts: PESA supersedes and completely replaces the Fifth Schedule provisions.
PESA extends Part IX of the Constitution with certain modifications to Fifth Schedule areas to ensure self-governance through Gram Sabhas.
PESA applies exclusively to Sixth Schedule states like Meghalaya and Mizoram.
PESA deals only with cooperative societies in urban tribal pockets.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Parliament enacted PESA, 1996 to extend the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution relating to Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule, giving sweeping powers of self-governance to Gram Sabhas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following taxation powers are uniquely vested in Autonomous District Councils under the Sixth Schedule?
opts: Power to levy and collect taxes on lands and buildings, and tolls on persons, subject to Governor's rules.
Power to levy corporate income tax and customs duties on international trade.
Power to levy GST across the entire state territory.
No taxation powers are given; they depend entirely on foreign aid.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Paragraph 8 of the Sixth Schedule, Autonomous District Councils have the power to assess and collect land revenue and impose taxes on lands, buildings, animals, vehicles, entry of goods, and professional taxes.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram treated differently under the Sixth Schedule compared to other tribal-dense states like Jharkhand or Chhattisgarh?
opts: Because tribal populations in the North-East have distinct cultural identities, historical isolation, and required autonomous local political structures to preserve their way of life.
Because peninsular states have higher literacy rates than north-eastern states.
Because the British never administered north-eastern hill tracts.
Because Fifth Schedule states do not have any tribal population.
practiceQuestions.sol: The north-eastern tribes covered under the Sixth Schedule had unique historical trajectories, being mostly excluded or partially excluded tracts under British rule, and needed robust autonomous local self-governing bodies (ADCs) to protect their distinct customs and land rights.

practiceQuestions.q: What role does the Governor play regarding the application of Acts of Parliament to Sixth Schedule areas?
opts: The Governor can direct that an Act of Parliament does not apply or applies with exceptions/modifications to an autonomous district or region.
The Governor can dissolve the Parliament if its laws conflict with tribal customs.
The Governor has no authority; all parliamentary laws apply automatically without modification.
The Governor must seek prior approval from the United Nations for any law exemption.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Paragraph 12A of the Sixth Schedule, acts of Parliament and the State Legislature do not automatically apply to autonomous districts and regions unless directed by the Governor with or without modifications/exceptions.

practiceQuestions.q: How are Commission reports on Scheduled Areas handled under Article 339 of the Indian Constitution?
opts: The President may at any time, and shall at the expiration of 10 years from the commencement of the Constitution, appoint a Commission to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas and welfare of STs.
The Supreme Court appoints a permanent tribunal every year to review tribal policies.
The Prime Minister submits an annual report exclusively to NITI Aayog.
State Governors report directly to foreign international organizations.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 339 provides that the President can appoint a commission at any time (and mandatorily after 10 years) to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes in the States. (e.g., Bhuria Commission, Xaxa Committee).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Scheduled Areas:
1. The criteria for declaring an area as a Scheduled Area include preponderance of tribal population, compactness and reasonable size of the area, and economic backwardness of the area.
2. The executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to the State as to the administration of the Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The criteria for declaring Scheduled Areas are laid down implicitly through practice and guidelines (preponderance of tribal population, compactness, viability, and economic backwardness relative to neighboring areas). Under Article 339(2), the executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to a State as to the drawing up and execution of schemes specified in the direction to be essential for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes in the State.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Tribal Advisory Councils (TAC) under the Fifth Schedule:
1. It is mandatory to establish a TAC in every state having Scheduled Areas.
2. All members of the TAC must be exclusively elected members of the State Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Paragraph 4 of the Fifth Schedule mandates that there shall be established in each State having Scheduled Areas a Tribal Advisory Council. Statement 2 is incorrect because while three-fourths of its members must be representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assembly, if the remaining members are insufficient, other members can be appointed from amongst the Scheduled Tribes residing in the area, not strictly requiring all to be MLAs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) under the Sixth Schedule:
1. ADCs have the power to make laws with respect to matters like land, forests, shifting cultivation, marriage, and social customs.
2. All laws made by ADCs on these matters require the mandatory assent of the Governor to come into force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Paragraph 3 of the Sixth Schedule, ADCs are empowered to make laws on land, forests, canal water, agriculture, shifting cultivation, town administration, inheritance of property, marriage, and social customs. However, Paragraph 3(3) explicitly mandates that all such laws made by a District Council shall submit to the Governor and shall have effect only when assented to by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Indian Constitution:
1. The Fifth Schedule applies to tribal areas in 10 states, whereas the Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in 4 states.
2. While the Fifth Schedule creates Advisory Councils, the Sixth Schedule establishes Autonomous District Councils and Regional Councils with legislative and judicial powers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Currently, Fifth Schedule areas exist in 10 states (Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana). Sixth Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. The structural distinction in statement 2 accurately reflects advisory vs. autonomous legislative/judicial bodies.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the alteration or creation of Scheduled Areas:
1. The Parliament of India can by law alter or declare any territory as a Scheduled Area without presidential intervention.
2. The Governor of a State has no role in proposing modifications to the boundaries of Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Under the Fifth Schedule, the power to declare an area as a Scheduled Area, alter its boundaries, increase, decrease, or rescind any notification rests solely with the President of India, acting after consultation with the Governor of the State. Parliament is not directly involved via standard statutory legislation for this purpose.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding financial autonomy of Autonomous District Councils under the Sixth Schedule:
1. ADCs are entirely funded by grants from the Consolidated Fund of India and cannot raise internal revenues.
2. The Governor may allocate a share of royalties accruing from licenses for mineral prospecting extracted within the autonomous district to the District Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because ADCs have independent taxation powers (levying land revenue, taxes on professions, trades, animals, vehicles, etc.). Statement 2 is correct: under Paragraph 9 of the Sixth Schedule, the share of royalties accruing each year from licenses or leases for mineral prospecting or extraction in autonomous districts is made payable to the District Council by the State Government as determined by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the applicability of laws to Scheduled and Tribal Areas:
1. The Governor can direct that any Central or State law shall not apply to a Fifth Schedule Scheduled Area.
2. Acts of Parliament relating to subjects specified by the Governor do not automatically extend to Sixth Schedule areas unless specific directions are given.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Fifth Schedule (Para 5), the Governor can exempt or modify the application of any Act of Parliament or State Legislature to Scheduled Areas. Under Sixth Schedule (Para 12 and 12A), acts of Parliament or State Legislature do not apply automatically to autonomous districts/regions unless directed by the Governor with/without modifications.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and nomination powers in Autonomous District Councils (ADCs):
1. All members of an ADC must be elected through direct adult suffrage without any nominated seats.
2. The Governor is empowered to nominate up to four members to an ADC to represent minority communities or unrepresented tribes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because an ADC is not composed purely of elected members; it has a mix. Statement 2 is correct: Paragraph 2(1) of the Sixth Schedule states that each Autonomous District Council consists of not more than 30 members, out of which not more than 4 are nominated by the Governor and the rest are elected on the basis of adult suffrage.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Commission of Inquiry / Reports on Scheduled Areas:
1. The President of India can appoint a Commission to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas at any time, and it is mandatory after 10 years of the commencement of the Constitution.
2. The historic Bhuria Committee (1995) recommendations formed the foundational blueprint for enacting the PESA Act, 1996.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 339(1) dictates the presidential power and the mandatory 10-year commission provision. The Bhuria Committee (Committee on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas), chaired by K.S. Bhuria in 1995, recommended giving wide self-governance powers to tribal communities, which directly led to the enactment of PESA, 1996.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Commission on Scheduled Areas under Article 339 and its operational scope:
1. The Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes Commission (1960), headed by V.N. Dhebar, was the first official commission appointed under Article 339.
2. The recommendations of Article 339 Commissions are legally binding on the Parliament and must be enacted into statutory laws within one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct in identifying the Dhebar Commission (1960-61) as the first Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes Commission appointed under Article 339(1). However, Statement 2 is incorrect because the recommendations made by such commissions are advisory/inquiry reports submitted to the President and laid before Parliament; they are not automatically legally binding nor mandated for statutory enactment within a strict one-year window.
